lead_with.title: Where the cells sit
lead_with.text: LVK301 aims to turn 'cold' tumours 'hot'. Proving that needs to know **where macrophages and T-cells sit** in the tumour before and after — SLACS isolates cells from exact regions (tumour core vs. edge) for sequencing.

lead_with.title: Better input for the AI
lead_with.text: Their AI picks gene targets from single-cell data. Region-specific single-cell data from CosmoSort can sharpen target selection.

lead_with.title: Small, partnered pilot
lead_with.text: Laverock is grant-funded and partnering. Offer a small data pilot or a joint grant application rather than an instrument sale.

person.name: Kevin Gillinder
person.text: Associate Director of Bioinformatics at Laverock Therapeutics (per Streak / LinkedIn). Public records show a **Kevin Gillinder, PhD** who studied transcription-factor gene regulation (KLF1, red blood cells) as a Research Fellow at **Monash University's Australian Centre for Blood Diseases** and was an ASHG trainee author — **to be confirmed** as the same person. He is direct and brief in messages and asked for a 'meeting planner'.

company.text: Laverock Therapeutics was set up in **2021** to commercialise the **gene editing–induced gene silencing (GEiGS®)** platform for human therapeutics. CEO **David Venables** previously founded Synpromics. Its programmable, tunable, multiplex silencing is applied to **T-cell and macrophage** therapies for solid tumours and to **hypoimmunogenic islet cells** for Type 1 diabetes. In Jun 2025 it said platform validation was complete and it was moving to lead-product selection, with better tumour control in models. In June 2026 it won **> £2.2M** in grants to scale the platform with single-cell data and AI for T-cell products and to extend macrophage programmes into non-oncology, via a consortium with academic and clinical partners.

financials.text: **Seed:** £13.5M (Oct 2023), extended to **> £20M** total (Jun 2025), led by Calculus Capital with Eli Lilly, Mercia Ventures, Maven Capital Partners, Eos Advisory, Norcliffe Capital, UK Innovation & Science Seed Fund, Tekfen Ventures. **Grants:** ~£1.8M from UKRI (Biomedical Catalyst, SMART, Investor Partnership) + **> £2.2M** (Jun 2026). Revenue: none disclosed (preclinical). Headcount to be confirmed.

industry.title: Solid tumours need spatial answers
industry.text: Cell therapies struggle in solid tumours because of the tumour microenvironment. Spatial data on immune cell location is becoming standard in these programmes.

industry.title: AI target discovery needs better data
industry.text: Single-cell atlases lose tissue position on dissociation. Spatially resolved, cell-level data is the next input layer for AI target selection.

talking_points: You use single-cell tumour data to pick gene-control targets — do you work with **dissociated scRNA-seq** only, or also spatial data?
For **LVK301**, how do you measure whether macrophages change the tumour from 'cold' to 'hot' — and where in the tumour?
Would **region-specific** single-cell data (tumour edge vs. core, near vs. far from T-cells) help your target selection?
Do you generate data in-house or through CROs and academic partners (e.g., the new grant consortium)?
Would a small **pilot dataset** on one of your tumour models be useful for the next grant milestone?
